text:
sam_infra: Quick proposal — add a short "holdback window" after a spot-backed scaleout where we intentionally keep X% capacity unfilled for Ys to absorb immediate eviction spikes. avoids reactive double-scaleouts.

mel: hmm interesting. want to sketch numbers?

sam_infra: idea: on scale-out event we mark N additional slots as "hedge-reserve" for 30s by not filling them from the queue until the window expires. config: `holdback_pct=10`, `holdback_window_s=30`.

nir: is that different from warm standby? sounds similar but transient.

sam_infra: yep lighter weight — no separate pool, just logical reservation inside existing mixed-capacity pools. cheaper than warm standby and fast to release.

jen: concern: if traffic is steady, reserving capacity will reduce throughput and increase queue time. when do we disable?

sam_infra: recommended heuristic: disable if queue length > Q_thresh or avg latency > L_thresh. otherwise default 30s then auto-release.

mel: can we tie holdback to interruption rate signal? e.g., if recent spot eviction rate > 0.5% in region, increase holdback_pct to 20%.

nir: good. also tie to region-specific preemption windows. some clouds have predictable maintenance patterns.

jen: show a quick config snippet and fallback rules?

sam_infra: sure — example:```yaml
# autoscaler holdback example
scale_policy:
  type: mixed_spot
  base_min: 20
  max_scale: 200
  holdback:
    enabled: true
    pct: 0.10            # fraction of newly added nodes to reserve
    window_s: 30         # reserve duration after scale-out
    queue_disable_threshold: 50
    latency_disable_ms: 250
    eviction_rate_scaleup: 0.005  # if eviction_rate > x, increase pct
    max_holdback_pct: 0.25
```

mel: what happens if reserved nodes get evicted? do we requeue them or immediately scale more?

sam_infra: policy: treat reserve nodes like regular nodes for eviction semantics. if reserve node evicted within window, don't trigger an immediate compensating scale-out; instead increase holdback window by +15s and trigger a slow-probe scale-up (cooldown 45s) to avoid thrash.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline check — sim test coverage required: eviction spike, steady high q, region failover.

nir: simulation notes: if holdback_pct too high under heavy steady load you'll see 8-12% extra queued latency; but it prevents 2x scale-out churn during 60s eviction cascades. tradeoff looks positive for latency-SLO workloads.

jen: I'd like to add an opt-in per-customer flag. enterprise customers with SLAs can set holdback_pct=0 and rely on reserved Dedicated.

sam_infra: agreed. default on public infra, but customer override allowed. also add metric: `holdback_releases` and `holdback_evictions` to console.

mel: one more tweak — when mixed-pool contains both spot and ondemand, prefer to mark ondemand instances as reserve first (if cost policy allows) to maintain throughput.

nir: careful, that can mask cost signal. add policy: only use ondemand for reserve if cost_budget_pct > 80% or in high-SLO routes.

sam_infra: next steps: PR with autoscaler changes + unit tests for config, e2e sim job with eviction trace. anyone volunteer to own sim job?

mel: I can iterate the sim scenarios this week.

jen: I'll do the PR for config + console metrics.

ops-bot: Reminder: ops playbook update needed for emergency scaleouts.

sam_infra: cool, thanks. I'll write up proposal doc and link sim traces. :thumbsup:
